message.content:
Looking at this question about the S118L mutation in Kir6.2 (an inward-rectifying potassium channel subunit that forms part of the KATP channel):

The S118 residue in Kir6.2 is located in the N-terminal cytoplasmic domain. This region is critical for proper channel folding and interaction with the SUR (sulfonylurea receptor) subunits. The S118L mutation has been shown to impair the forward trafficking of the KATP channel from the endoplasmic reticulum/Golgi to the plasma membrane. This means fewer functional channels reach the cell surface, reducing potassium conductance at the membrane.

This is distinct from directly altering ATP sensitivity (option C) or affecting metabolic inhibition (option A). The primary impact of this specific mutation is on the trafficking pathway of the channel protein to the membrane.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
